description: Non-code third-party files DISTRIBUTED inside Domowik binaries, per docs/THIRD-PARTY-POLICY.md. Cargo dependencies are recorded separately in docs/RUST-DEPENDENCIES.md and NOTICE; this file exists because a font is neither a crate nor a dev tool, so neither of those generators can see it. scripts/rust-notice.py reads this file and reproduces each licence text into NOTICE, and scripts/verify.sh diffs the result, so an asset added without a record here fails the build.

assets.name: Noto Sans Regular
assets.usedIn: crates/domowik-cli/src/label.rs; embedded with include_bytes! and used for room-name glyph outlines in SVG and PNG export (BEHAVIOR-SPEC R5.3.3, issue 0060)
assets.provenance: Downloaded 2026-09-12 from the notofonts distribution repository at the pinned commit, unmodified and unsubset. The built binaries are published there; the font project's own sources and the OFL text live in the upstream repository, whose tag NotoSans-v2.015 matches the version this binary's name table reports (uniqueID 2.015;GOOG;NotoSans-Regular). The licence text committed beside the font is that tag's OFL.txt. The file's own name table records the licence at IDs 13 and 14, which agrees. The unhinted build is chosen deliberately: hinting is grid-fitting for small-size rasterisation and Domowik reads outlines, so the hints would be 190 KB of bytes nothing consults.
assets.obligations: OFL-1.1 requires the licence and copyright notice to travel with the font, which NOTICE and the committed OFL text satisfy; it forbids selling the font by itself, which Domowik does not do. The font carries NO Reserved Font Name, so modification and renaming are unrestricted — but this copy is unmodified and should stay so, since modifying it would move the provenance record from a download to a tool run.
assets.review: OFL-1.1 is not on the dependency allow-list in scripts/rust-deps-inventory.py, which does not assess bundled assets. It is a permissive font licence with an attribution obligation and no copyleft reach into Domowik's own code: the font is aggregated, not linked, and OFL section 2 binds only the Font Software. Adopted on explicit direction from the orchestrating agent (root), 2026-09-12, which is where the dependency decision sits; the OWNER has not ratified OFL-1.1 as a licence family for distributed assets, and this record must not be read as saying they have. If asset licences are added to the dependency allow-list, this entry is the one to re-review.

assets.name: Roboto Regular
assets.copyright: Copyright 2011 Google Inc. All Rights Reserved.
assets.usedIn: The browser editor only: frontend/scripts/build-web-modules.sh copies it, unmodified, with its licence as LICENSE.txt, to fallback-fonts/roboto/v32/KFOmCnqEu92Fr1Me4GZLCzYlKw.woff2 in the web bundle (where CanvasKit loads Roboto under the page-relative fontFallbackBaseUrl) and to the same path under assets/ (where skwasm loads it); declared in release/rust-manifest.json copiedAssets. Named as the text family by frontend/lib/editor_fonts.dart (ADR 0012 section 6, ED-0121). Not a pubspec font, so no native bundle carries it.
assets.provenance: Downloaded 2026-10-13 from the release v2.138 of googlefonts/roboto-2 (formerly googlefonts/roboto; the tag object 0e11861ecb9e6ce4336f47b556f3d12ba72c3f46 points at the commit recorded here). The release zip's Roboto-Regular.ttf is copied unmodified and unsubset; the licence text beside it is the zip's LICENSE, the Apache License 2.0 verbatim. The name table reports Version 2.138 and records the licence at IDs 13 and 14 as Apache-2.0, which agrees. 2.138 is the last Apache-2.0 Roboto release; the later Roboto 3 is under OFL-1.1 and was not chosen. Flutter's web engine otherwise downloads Roboto 2.137 Regular from fonts.gstatic.com; the bundled 2.138 maps every code point that file maps (checked with fontTools on 2026-10-13), plus more.
assets.obligations: Apache-2.0, Domowik's own licence: the licence text travels with the font in NOTICE and as LICENSE.txt beside each copy in the web bundle. The release ships no NOTICE file of its own to reproduce.
assets.review: Same licence as Domowik; no new licence family. Bundled on the owner's instruction of 2026-10-13 (ED-0121).

assets.name: Noto Sans Symbols 2 Subset
assets.usedIn: frontend/pubspec.yaml font family 'Noto Sans Symbols 2 Subset', shipped in the Flutter asset bundle of the web and desktop builds, with frontend/assets/fonts/NotoSansSymbols2-NOTICES.txt (package name, blank line, the OFL text) listed under flutter: licenses so assets/NOTICES carries it. Named only by the browser editor, as the fallback family of the theme and painter text styles, for 'Command (⌘)' and user text (frontend/lib/editor_fonts.dart, BEHAVIOR-SPEC 11.2, ADR 0012 section 6, ED-0121).
assets.provenance: Downloaded 2026-10-13 from the notofonts distribution repository at the same pinned commit as the Noto Sans Regular entry. The upstream tag NotoSansSymbols2-v2.008 (commit 25b00f0d3f40873a005287514ba2a48558655314) matches the version the name table reports; the licence text committed beside the font is that tag's OFL.txt. MODIFIED by subsetting to the single code point U+2318 with fontTools 4.66.1: `pyftsubset NotoSansSymbols2-Regular.ttf --unicodes=U+2318 --name-IDs='*' --name-languages='*' --name-legacy --notdef-outline --output-file=NotoSansSymbols2-Subset.ttf`. Two runs gave byte-identical output. Every name record is kept, so the file still states its copyright and licence at IDs 0, 13 and 14. The whole font is 672 KB, and Google Fonts' own subset containing U+2318 is 383 KB; the subset is 2.2 KB.
assets.obligations: OFL-1.1: the licence and copyright notice travel with the font, in NOTICE, in the committed OFL text, and in each built bundle's assets/NOTICES. A Modified Version must stay under the OFL and must not use a Reserved Font Name; the font declares none, so keeping its name is permitted. The font is not sold by itself.
assets.review: Same licence family and upstream as the Noto Sans Regular entry. Bundled on the owner's instruction of 2026-10-13 to bundle the browser editor's fonts (ED-0121); the subsetting is a Domowik tool run, recorded above, so re-derive it from the upstream file rather than editing it.
